items.title: hikari-risa
items.text: Components V2 views for hikari, with state that survives restarts.

items.title: risa.codecs
items.text:
How InMessage state is written into custom_id characters.

BASE85, the default, is built in and keeps every character printable ASCII. BASE32768 and URO14 come with the [radixly] extra and carry more than twice as many bytes per character.

items.title: RADIXLY_EXTRA module-attribute
items.text:
RADIXLY_EXTRA = 'radixly'

The name of the extra (hikari-risa[radixly]) that BASE32768 and URO14 need.

items.title: BASE85 module-attribute
items.text:
BASE85 = Codec(tag='a', name='base85', encode=_b85_encode, decode=_b85_decode, max_bytes=_b85_max_bytes)

The default codec: printable ASCII, built in, needs no extra.

items.title: BASE32768 module-attribute
items.text:
BASE32768 = _radixly('w', 'base32768')

15 bits per character, the densest codec; needs the [radixly] extra.

items.title: URO14 module-attribute
items.text:
URO14 = _radixly('u', 'uro14')

14 bits per CJK character behind a length prefix; needs the [radixly] extra.

items.title: Codec
items.text:
Bases: Struct

A way of writing bytes as custom_id characters.

Attributes:

  • tag (str) –

    One character, written ahead of the state, that names the codec on the wire.

  • name (str) –

    A human-readable name for messages and logs.

  • encode (Callable[[bytes], str]) –

    Turns bytes into text.

  • decode (Callable[[str], bytes]) –

    Turns that text back into the same bytes.

  • max_bytes (Callable[[int], int]) –

    How many bytes fit into a given number of characters.

items.title: Contexts
items.text:
The linkd contexts risa dispatches in.

A handler runs inside DEFAULT with COMPONENT entered on top, so it can be injected with anything registered in either. risa adds the ComponentContext and the hikari.ComponentInteraction to COMPONENT for every click.

Attributes:

    linkd's root context, the one a lightbulb client shares.

  • MODAL (Final) –

    Reserved for modal submissions.

items.title: risa.errors
items.text:
The exceptions risa raises.

Every exception derives from RisaError, builds its own message, and keeps the details it was raised with as attributes, so callers can branch on fields instead of parsing the message.

items.title: SignatureMismatchError
items.text:
Bases: RisaError

Logged, not raised, when a click carries wire arguments for another handler signature.

The handler's wire parameters changed without a version bump. risa logs this error and routes the click to View.on_outdated. Bump the version in @risa.handler(version=...) so the old components are retired instead.

Attributes:

    The view the handler belongs to.

  • handler_id –

    The handler's id.

  • version –

    The handler's version.

  • found –

    The fingerprint the component carries.

  • expected –

    The fingerprint of the handler's current signature.

items.title: EphemeralOriginError
items.text:
Bases: RisaError

Raised when an ephemeral origin message can no longer be edited.

On an ephemeral view, rerender() and edit() must be the initial response, or follow a silent defer().

Attributes:

items.text:

Raised when an InMessage view's durable state does not fit its components.

Attributes:

  • slots –

  • codec_name –

    The codec the state was written with.

  • fields (Mapping[str, int]) –

    The bytes each durable field takes, by name, in declaration order. What they leave of needed is risa's own framing.

items.title: StateConflictError
items.text:
Bases: StateError

Raised when another process wrote a view's state first.

By the time it is raised, the view already holds the state that won, so the handler can apply its change again on top of it.

items.title: StoreUnavailableError
items.text:
Bases: StateError

Raised when the store holding a view's state cannot be reached.

The state is not lost; it only cannot be read or written right now. A store reports missing state by returning nothing, never with this error.

Attributes:

  • reason –

    What went wrong.

    One line per failed check, naming the check and what went wrong.

items.title: risa
items.text:
A component handler for hikari, built on Discord's Components V2.

A view is a class whose fields are its state, whose render returns its layout, and whose handlers answer the clicks on it. The state travels inside the message by default, so views survive restarts with no infrastructure, or lives in a store for views that outgrow it.

items.title: bind module-attribute
items.text:
bind = functools.partial

Put a handler on a component together with its wire arguments.

ui.Button(risa.bind(self.vote, 2)) routes a click on that button to vote(ctx, 2). It is functools.partial, so arguments go by position or by name, and nested bind calls merge as partials do: a keyword given twice takes the outer value.

items.title: BindTarget
items.text: BindTarget = Callable[P, Awaitable[None]]

items.title: HandlerFunction
items.text: HandlerFunction = Callable[Concatenate[V, ComponentContext, P], Awaitable[None]]

items.title: Handlerish
items.text: Handlerish = Callable[..., Awaitable[None]] | Binding | partial[Awaitable[None]]

items.title: AutoDefer
items.text:
Bases: StrEnum

How risa answers a click whose handler has not answered in time.

Discord fails an interaction that gets no answer within three seconds. With auto-defer, risa acknowledges the click in the handler's place after the client's auto_defer_delay, and the handler carries on. Set it on the client, on a view with @risa.register(defer=...), or on a handler with @risa.handler(defer=...); the most specific setting wins.

Attributes:

  • OFF –

    Never answer in the handler's place. The default.

  • UPDATE –

    Acknowledge silently, for a handler that answers with ctx.rerender() or ctx.edit(...).

  • THINKING –

    Show a "thinking..." message, for a handler that answers with ctx.respond(...), which then takes its place.

  • THINKING_EPHEMERAL –

    The same, visible only to the user who clicked.

items.title: Binding
items.text:
Bases: Struct

A handler resolved for one component: where a click routes, and what it carries.

Components resolve the handler they are given into one; it is rarely built by hand.

Attributes:

  • handler_id (str) –

    The id of the handler.

  • version (int) –

    The version of the handler.

  • token (str) –

    The routing token of the handler.

  • fingerprint (str) –

    The hash of the handler's wire signature, empty without wire arguments.

  • frames (Sequence[Frame]) –

    The encoded wire arguments.

  • func_name (str) –

    The handler's qualified name, for messages.

  • owner (type[View] | None) –

    The view class the handler is defined on.

items.title: Client
items.text:
Bases: ABC

Routes clicks on registered views to their handlers.

Make one with client_from_app or client_from_lightbulb, add views with add_view, and send a view with build. A client answers only custom_ids risa wrote, so it can share a bot with other component handlers.

Parameters:

  • use_global (bool, default: False ) –

    Also route views registered with @risa.register but never added to this client.

  • di (DependencyInjectionManager | None, default: None ) –

    The linkd manager handlers are injected from; a new one by default.

  • register_app_dependencies (bool, default: True ) –

    Register the app, its REST client, and its event manager or interaction server for injection.

  • auto_defer (AutoDefer, default: OFF ) –

    The AutoDefer of views and handlers that set none, OFF by default.

  • auto_defer_delay (float, default: AUTO_DEFER_DELAY ) –

    Seconds after which auto-defer answers a click in its handler's place.

  • store (Store | None, default: None ) –

    The store InStore views use unless they name another.

  • stores (Mapping[str, Store] | None, default: None ) –

    Further stores, by the name InStore(store=...) refers to them by.

  • key_prefix (str | None, default: None ) –

    The prefix of every store key, risa:{application id} by default. Set it to fit a Redis ACL pattern, or to separate bots that share one store.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If key_prefix is blank, or the default store is given both as store and in stores.

items.title: build async
items.text:
build(view)

Render view into the components of a new message, ready to send.

await ctx.respond(**await client.build(Poll(question="Ship it?")))

It runs the view's load, renders it, and writes an InStore view's first record. The result spreads into any hikari or lightbulb call that takes components=. If that send fails, the record stays behind until its TTL reaps it, or for good under InStore(ttl=None).

Returns:

  • Rendered –

    The components, as a mapping that spreads into a send.

Raises:

  • NotAViewError –

    If the view's class was never registered.

  • ViewDeclarationError –

    If the view keeps its state in a store this client does not have.

  • StateOverflowError –

    If an InMessage view's state does not fit its components.

Raises:

    If the class was never registered.

  • ViewDeclarationError –

    If the view keeps its state in a store this client does not have.

items.title: ComponentContext
items.text:
Bases: Context[ComponentInteraction]

The context of a click on one of a view's components.

A handler answers through it: rerender() redraws the message from the view's state, edit(...) replaces it with another layout, and respond(...) sends a new message.

items.title: message property
items.text:
message

The message the component is on, if any.

items.title: values property
items.text:
values

The values picked in a select menu; empty for a button.

items.title: resolved property
items.text:
resolved

The users, members, roles and channels picked in an entity select menu, or None.

items.title: edit async
items.text:
edit(layout)

Replace the message with layout, keeping the view's state on it.

For a screen the view's render does not draw, such as a confirmation or a closing message. A layout without interactive components ends the view, since nothing on it can be clicked any more. Like rerender(), it saves the view's state.

Raises:

  • NoViewError –

    If the layout has interactive components but this context has no view state, as in on_outdated and on_state_missing.

  • EphemeralOriginError –

    If the message is ephemeral and the interaction was answered with a new message.

  • StateOverflowError –

    If an InMessage view's state does not fit the layout's components.

  • StateConflictError –

    If another process saved the view's state first. The view then holds that state.

items.title: rerender async
items.text:
rerender()

Redraw the message from the view's current state, and save that state.

Every rerender is a commit. InMessage state is written into the message itself; InStore state goes to the store first, then the message is edited. A change made without calling it is saved when the handler returns, but that save can only log a failure; call it yourself, before any respond(), where a failure must be handled.

Raises:

  • NoViewError –

    If the view has durable fields but this context has no view state, as in on_outdated and on_state_missing.

  • EphemeralOriginError –

    If the message is ephemeral and the interaction was answered with a new message.

  • StateOverflowError –

    If an InMessage view's state no longer fits its components.

  • StateConflictError –

    If another process saved the view's state first. The view then holds that state, and the handler can apply its change again and rerender.

  • StateNotFoundError –

    If an InStore view's record disappeared while the handler ran.

items.title: defer async
items.text:
defer(*, thinking=False, ephemeral=False)

Acknowledge the interaction now and answer it later.

By default the acknowledgement is silent, and the answer is a rerender() or an edit() of the message. With thinking=True, Discord shows a "thinking..." message that the next respond() takes the place of.

Parameters:

  • thinking (bool, default: False ) –

    Show a "thinking..." message.

  • ephemeral (bool, default: False ) –

    Show that message only to the user who clicked.

Raises:

  • AlreadyRespondedError –

    If the interaction already has its initial response.

items.title: acknowledge async
items.text:
acknowledge(*, thinking=False, ephemeral=False)

Acknowledge the interaction like defer, unless it already has its initial response.

Where defer raises, this does nothing, so it is safe to call whatever happened before.

items.title: View
items.text:
Bases: Struct

Base class of a view: a message's layout, its state, and the handlers behind it.

A view is a msgspec.Struct, and its annotated fields are its durable state, carried from click to click. Mark a field risa.Prop[...] to rebuild it fresh on every click instead, typically in load. Register the class with @risa.register, return its layout from render, and send it with client.build:

@risa.register(name="counter")
class Counter(risa.View):
    count: int = 0

    def render(self) -> ui.Layout:
        return ui.Row(ui.Button(self.add, label=f"Clicked {self.count} times"))

    @risa.handler
    async def add(self, ctx: risa.ComponentContext) -> None:
        self.count += 1
        await ctx.rerender()

Each click runs its handler on the latest saved state of its view, and clicks on one view queue up within a process, each waiting up to ten seconds for the lock; one that waits longer is logged and goes unanswered. A view without durable fields has nothing to protect and takes no lock, so its handlers may run at the same time. Across processes, an InStore view on a shared store lets the first write win, while for an InMessage view the last edit of the message wins. A change made without ctx.rerender() is saved when the handler returns, but that save can only log a failure, so a handler that must know calls ctx.rerender() itself, before any ctx.respond(). A handler that raises keeps what it saved through rerender() or edit() before, and loses the rest.

items.title: render
items.text:
render()

Return the view's layout, drawn from its current state.

It runs for the first send and for every rerender. Keep it synchronous and free of I/O; fetch what it shows in load.

items.title: load async
items.text:
load()

Fill the view's props before it renders.

risa awaits it before the first send and on every click, after restoring the durable state and before the handler runs. Its parameters are injected, as a handler's are.

items.title: on_outdated async classmethod
items.text:
on_outdated(ctx)

Answer a click on a component this view can no longer route.

The component's handler was retired by a version bump, its wire parameters changed without one, or its state was written by durable fields the view no longer has. The default does nothing, so the click fails on the user's side, and risa logs it. Override it to answer the user, or to replace the dead message with ctx.edit(...). Its parameters are injected, as a handler's are, and ctx has no view state.

To answer clicks on one retired handler differently, keep a method with its id, version and wire parameters whose body says the component is outdated. It routes like any handler, and nothing is logged.

items.title: handler
items.text:
handler(func: HandlerFunction[V, P]) -> HandlerMethod[V, P]

handler(*, handler_id: str | None = ..., version: int = ..., defer: AutoDefer | None = ...) -> _HandlerDecorator

handler(func=None, /, *, handler_id=None, version=1, defer=None)

Make a view method a handler that components can route to.

Use it bare or with options. A handler takes the view and a ComponentContext, then its wire parameters, then anything to inject:

@risa.handler(defer=risa.AutoDefer.UPDATE)
async def vote(
    self, ctx: risa.ComponentContext, option: int, db: Database
) -> None: ...

Wire parameters come first, are positional, and are annotated bool, int, str, hikari.Snowflake or an enum.Enum of int or str values. They receive the values risa.bind put on the component. Every parameter after them is injected through linkd, so a hikari enum such as hikari.ChannelType, which is not an enum.Enum, is injected too; to carry one on the wire, bind its value as an int. A handler returns None.

Parameters:

  • handler_id (str | None, default: None ) –

    The id the handler routes under, the method's name by default. Pin it before renaming the method, so components already sent keep working.

  • version (int, default: 1 ) –

    Bump it when the wire parameters change. Components sent before keep routing to a method that still has the old version; once none does, they go to View.on_outdated.

  • defer (AutoDefer | None, default: None ) –

    The handler's AutoDefer, overriding the view's.

Returns:

  • HandlerMethod | Callable[[HandlerFunction], HandlerMethod] –

    The handler, or a decorator that makes one when options are given.

items.title: register
items.text:
register(*, name, version=1, defer=None, state=DEFAULT_PLACEMENT)

Register a view class so its components can be routed.

@risa.register(name="poll", state=risa.InStore(ttl=30 * 86400))
class Poll(risa.View): ...

A client then routes it once it is passed to client.add_view. The decorator raises ViewDeclarationError for a class risa cannot serve, such as a blank name, a prop without a default, or an InStore view without durable fields.

Parameters:

  • name (str) –

    The name the view routes under. Renaming it retires every component already sent.

  • version (int, default: 1 ) –

    The schema version of the durable state. Appending fields that have defaults needs no bump; any other change to the durable fields does, and components sent before the bump no longer route to the view.

  • defer (AutoDefer | None, default: None ) –

    The view's AutoDefer, for handlers that set none.

  • state (StatePlacement, default: DEFAULT_PLACEMENT ) –

    Where the durable state lives: InMessage(), the default, or InStore(...).

Returns:

  • Callable[[type[T]], type[T]] –

    The decorator. It returns the class unchanged.

items.title: InMessage
items.text:
Bases: Struct

Keep a view's durable state inside the message it renders.

The default placement. The state is written into the spare characters of the rendered components' custom_ids and read back from the message on every click. It needs no infrastructure, survives restarts, and lives exactly as long as the message. It is bounded by what the components can carry: up to about 70 bytes per interactive component with the default codec.

The state is readable by anyone who can see the message, and a client can forge it. Never keep secrets in durable fields, and never base an authorization decision on one alone.

Attributes:

  • codec (Codec) –

    How the state is written into custom_ids. risa.codecs.BASE85 by default; BASE32768 and URO14 from the [radixly] extra carry more than twice as much.

items.title: InStore
items.text:
Bases: Struct

Keep a view's durable state in a store, under a key the message carries.

The components carry only a random key, and the state is one record in the client's store of the name store. It has no size bound, every process of a bot shares it through a distributed store, and it expires.

Attributes:

  • ttl (float | None) –

    Seconds an untouched record lives. Every click restarts the clock, so only abandoned views expire. None keeps records forever, including the ones a deleted message or a failed send leaves behind. There is no default, since no lifetime suits both a confirmation dialog and a role menu.

  • store (str) –

    Which of the client's stores holds the state: "default" for the client's store=, or a key of its stores=.

items.title: DEFAULT_MAX_HOLD module-attribute

items.title: DEFAULT_TABLE module-attribute
items.text:
DEFAULT_TABLE = 'risa_state'

The name of the state table when none is given.

items.title: PostgresStore
items.text:
Bases: Store

A store on PostgreSQL, through an asyncpg pool.

An entry is a row of table. lock() takes a lease on a row of {table}_lease and renews it while held, so clicks on one view queue up across every process that shares the database. The store creates both tables on first use if they are missing, and deletes expired rows itself: on its first write, then on every hundredth.

Parameters:

  • pool (Pool) –

    The pool the bot owns. The store borrows a connection for each statement and never opens or closes the pool.

  • table (str, default: DEFAULT_TABLE ) –

    The name of the state table: a lowercase identifier of at most 52 characters. The lease table is named after it.

  • lease (float, default: DEFAULT_LEASE ) –

    Seconds a lock's lease lasts. It is renewed every third of that while held, and a crashed holder blocks its view for at most this long.

  • max_hold (float, default: DEFAULT_MAX_HOLD ) –

    Seconds after which a held lock is no longer renewed, so a stuck handler cannot block its view for good.

Raises:

  • ValueError –

    If table is not a plain lowercase identifier, lease is not positive, or max_hold is shorter than lease.

Hold key exclusively while the returned context manager is entered.

items.title: verify_store async
items.text:
verify_store(store)

Check that store behaves the way risa relies on.

Seventeen checks cover round trips, versions, the compare-and-set, expiry, touch and the lock. They run concurrently, each on its own random key under risa:conformance:, and each deletes what it wrote. Run it against a real instance of the backend, from a test or a script; it needs no test framework.

Raises:

  • StoreConformanceError –

    If any check fails. It lists every failure, not just the first.

items.title: Store
items.text:
Bases: Protocol

Where risa keeps the state of InStore views.

Implement it to keep state somewhere risa ships no store for, and check the implementation with risa.store.testing.verify_store. A missing or expired entry is never an error: it reads as None.
